summary: Verified the bug fix for the silent-exit issue in /app/scripts/spoof-tunnel.sh (load_config + 'set -euo pipefail' interaction). All four verification phases pass: (A) with NO config file the manager reaches the whiptail menu, (B) with a config file containing PUB_IFACE the manager also reaches the whiptail menu (this is the fix), (C) the new load_config() implementation is itself errexit-safe, (D) the original buggy pattern is confirmed to abort silently under 'set -e'. Also re-verified installer syntax, NEEDRESTART env vars, and the broken-apt-repo resilience regression tests.

tests_executed.name: grep for 'set -o pipefail' and absence of 'set -e'/'set -eu'/'set -euo' in /app/scripts/spoof-tunnel.sh
tests_executed.details: Line 13 is exactly 'set -o pipefail'. No line matches ^set -(e|eu|euo)($|[^o]). The dangerous errexit/nounset flags are gone from the interactive TUI script.

tests_executed.name: install.sh dependency install line uses NEEDRESTART_MODE=l NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1
tests_executed.details: Confirmed at /app/install.sh:53 -> 'DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive NEEDRESTART_MODE=l NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1 apt-get install ...'. Also present at /app/scripts/spoof-tunnel.sh:118 (do_install). This prevents SSH disconnects triggered by needrestart's default interactive mode during apt on Ubuntu 22.04+.

tests_executed.details: Stubbed whiptail on PATH; the manager successfully calls it after load_config() (marker recorded with '--title Spoof-Tunnel Manager --menu ...'). Baseline behavior preserved.

tests_executed.name: test_load_config_fix.sh Phase B: config file WITH PUB_IFACE -> reaches whiptail (THE FIX)
tests_executed.details: Wrote /etc/spoof-tunnel/config with PUB_IFACE="eth0", ROLE="relay", CARRIER="udp" and re-ran. Under the OLD 'set -euo pipefail' + '[[ -z "$PUB_IFACE" ]] && ...' code this exited silently before the menu; now the whiptail stub was invoked AND the marker shows '[relay] carrier=udp ...' meaning the config was actually sourced and applied. Bug fix verified.

tests_executed.details: Ran the new load_config() body inside 'set -euo pipefail'. It returns 0 and preserves PUB_IFACE=eth0 from the sourced file.

tests_executed.name: test_load_config_fix.sh Phase D: reproduce the original bug
tests_executed.details: Recreated a function ending in '[[ -z "$PUB_IFACE" ]] && PUB_IFACE="fallback"' with PUB_IFACE="eth0" pre-set, under 'set -euo pipefail'. The bash process exits rc=1 without reaching the line after the function call — confirming the root cause exactly as reported.

After my fix (see updated_files) the zz-broken-test2.list is now cleaned up correctly on exit.

critical_code_review_comments: /app/scripts/spoof-tunnel.sh: the rationale comment (lines 9-12) for dropping 'set -e'/'set -u' from an interactive whiptail TUI is correct — whiptail Cancel/ESC returns non-zero, 'iptables -C' returns non-zero on absence, and '[[ ]] && cmd' constructs routinely return non-zero. Errexit here would cause exactly the kind of silent-exit reported.

/app/scripts/spoof-tunnel.sh:70-78 load_config(): now uses explicit if-blocks and ends with 'return 0'. This is safe even if a future maintainer re-enables 'set -e' on the top-level script, so the fix is defensive.

/app/install.sh:53: adding NEEDRESTART_MODE=l NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1 is the correct mitigation for the well-known Ubuntu 22.04+ needrestart pop-up that can restart sshd mid-install and disconnect the operator. Good change.

/app/install.sh keeps 'set -euo pipefail' — that IS correct for a non-interactive installer where any failing step should abort. Only the interactive TUI script needed the flag removed. Nice separation.

Minor test hygiene (already fixed by me): /app/tests/test_install_deps_missing.sh previously called 'exit 1' inside a function, which prevented the outer cleanup 'rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/zz-broken-test2.list' from running. Changed to 'return 1' so the cleanup line now executes on every path.

Container limitation (expected, NOT a bug): CAP_NET_RAW is not granted in this Kubernetes pod, so the C core's raw-socket run/probe modes cannot be exercised end-to-end here. Only the bug fix logic and the installer harness are testable in this environment — both pass.

context_for_next_testing_agent: This is a CLI/network tool (Pure C core + bash installer + whiptail TUI). No HTTP endpoints. Do NOT use curl/playwright. Reusable regression scripts: /app/tests/test_load_config_fix.sh (verifies the load_config/set -e silent-exit fix), /app/tests/test_install_deps.sh (broken-repo happy path), /app/tests/test_install_deps_missing.sh (broken-repo ERROR path). Container is aarch64, no CAP_NET_RAW — raw-socket and WireGuard flows are not exercisable here. Always run as root. The whiptail stub trick used in test_load_config_fix.sh is the correct way to prove the TUI script reaches its menu without needing a real terminal.
rca of the issue: Original bug: running 'spoof-tunnel' after menu option 1 (Install & auto-setup) silently returned to the shell prompt with no menu. Root cause: /app/scripts/spoof-tunnel.sh had 'set -euo pipefail'; load_config()'s last statement was `[[ -z "$PUB_IFACE" ]] && PUB_IFACE="$(detect_pub_iface || true)"`. After menu 1 saved a config with PUB_IFACE populated, sourcing that config left PUB_IFACE non-empty, so `[[ -z "$PUB_IFACE" ]]` returned 1 — which became load_config()'s exit status. Under 'set -e', a function returning non-zero when called at top-level aborts the whole script. Result: script exited between load_config and main_menu with no message, so 'spoof-tunnel' appeared to do nothing. Fix (already applied by main agent, verified here): (1) change line 13 from 'set -euo pipefail' to 'set -o pipefail' — appropriate because this is an interactive whiptail menu where many benign non-zero returns occur (Cancel/ESC, existence checks, guard idioms), and (2) rewrite load_config() to use explicit if-blocks and end with 'return 0' so it can never return non-zero even if reintroduced under strict mode. Verified: Phase B of /app/tests/test_load_config_fix.sh now reaches the whiptail menu with ROLE=relay applied from the config, and Phase D reproduces the original failure exactly.
